# Resource proposals for the protocol's resources table

Wrote `benchmark/resources-proposal.md` with one entry for each of the seven rows. Each entry gives what it unblocks, resource options, owner questions, which providers see which data, access, publication and revocation terms, owner steps, a git/python3 readiness check, and whether ordinary public work can cover it.

An earlier session reported writing this file, but it was not on disk when I checked (a read returned FileNotFoundError), so I rewrote it in this session.

Rows 1 (restricted store) and 2 (native job runner) are the most developed. Row 7 (reviewers and scorer) needs no new access for public review. Rows 1, 4 and 5 cannot be satisfied by public work.

Licence types, LabVIEW versions and modules, providers, custodians, quota and retention settings are listed as owner questions. Spending is marked as needing a specific owner grant with a ceiling.

I did not edit `benchmark/protocol.md` or `benchmark/preparation.json`. The proposal sets no thresholds, does not choose the 2024 fallback, narrows no scope and claims no readiness. I did not run the readiness checks. I also did not run the verification command; the file is well over 200 characters.

## What next

The Policymaker picks a row (1 and 2 first), fills in the actual resources and providers from the owner answers, and files a `capability` request. Do not treat the proposal as a grant; wait for provisioning and `capability-ready`.

Waiting for the owner: request #161.
